references.text: The first census in the wilderness counted the tribe of Simeon as 59,300 men. Here in the second census, the number has dropped to 22,200, showing a dramatic decline in the size of the tribe.
Lists the sons of Simeon who went to Egypt with Jacob; these became the ancestors of the clans mentioned in the tribe of Simeon.
Mentions the sons of Simeon and their clans, which form the basis for the genealogical divisions in the census.
The plague that struck Israel at Baal-Peor killed 24,000 people. The tribe of Simeon may have been especially hard hit, which could explain the large drop in population.
Zimri, son of Salu, was a leader in the tribe of Simeon who was killed along with the Midianite woman. This shows that the tribe of Simeon was involved in the sin at Baal-Peor.
1 Chronicles confirms that the tribe of Simeon remained small compared to Judah, consistent with the census here.
